questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code serializes or deserializes webhook payloads and money values? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The provider starts sending a new signed event {"id":"evt_9","type":"dispute.opened","occurredAt":"2025-03-01T10:00:00Z","disputeId":"dp_1"}. What does handle return and what happens to the event?
choices: 400, because the type has no registered subtype and deserialization fails
500, because the unknown type throws an unchecked exception out of handle
200; it is deserialized as Unknown and is not passed to the sink
200; it is passed to the sink as a Succeeded event with null fields

questions.prompt: A validly signed refund.created event has amount {"amount":"10.505","currency":"USD"}. What does handle return?
choices: 200; the amount is rounded to 10.51 by setScale
400; Money.parse throws, which surfaces as a Jackson exception caught as IOException
401; the amount does not match the signature

questions.prompt: Why is the signature computed over rawBody rather than over a re-serialized event?
choices: Because Jackson cannot serialize sealed interfaces back to JSON
Because re-serializing the parsed object could change bytes (field order, number formatting, dropped unknown fields), so the HMAC would not match what the provider signed
Because MessageDigest.isEqual only accepts byte arrays that come directly from the network
Because parsing first would make the Unknown fallback impossible
